title: Known linear-response tools remain the ordinary comparator
statement: For Gaussian A=A0+BDB^T>0,b=b0+Bg, retained baseline solves and response matrices yield means/covariances through the ordinary Woodbury/Schur reduced system, with O(r^3+mr) mean-query work and paid baseline factorization/storage; rank r may grow to ambientN. A separately supplied residual sketch theorem fixes A0,dictionaryB,basisV,f0 BEFORE a Gaussian sketch. Uniform union-of-subspaces control for supports<=s of residual dimension<=k+s+1 permits unlimited adaptive updates within that family, with d>=32/epsilon^2[(k+s+1)log9+s log(e r/s)+log(2/delta)]. Known A>=alpha I gives output error<=||c||||S residual||/[alpha sqrt(1-epsilon)]. Basis/dictionary discovery,offline sketch applications and storageO(dr) are paid; accumulated local edits may leave the certified sparse family, and a passing certificate is not guaranteed for every input. These supplied derivations credit ordinary reduced-order/pyMOR-style residual estimators and do not establish an advantage.

requires: For Gaussian reuse: fixed SPD baseline, supplied low-rank response span/output directions and updates preserving SPD, with baseline factorization/solves paid.
For residual sketches: fixed baseline,dictionary,basis and right-hand side BEFORE the random sketch, known coercivity lower bound and at most the certified sparse support size.
Adaptive queries stay in that same uniformly certified union of subspaces; sketch randomness cannot be used to fit an uncertified new basis/dictionary.

assumptions: These are ordinary Woodbury/reduced-order response and residual constructions, not a new efficiency advantage. Accumulating local edits can leave the certified sparse family; a low-dimensional bound need not pass the desired tolerance.
costs: After responses are constructed, scalar uniform error is an O(K^2) pairwise optimization; finite-target TV can use O(q log q) sign/root work per pair in exact real arithmetic, with numerical isolation/bit costs separately paid.

Exact-mass scalar coarsening sorts K values in O(K log K); retaining masses/assignments still costs O(K),a dense coefficient query costsOmega(K),and an equally informed exact scalar baseline already supports O(s) changed-coefficient updates.

Dynamic q-state chains readTheta(nq^2) entries,buildO(nq^3),storeO(nq^2),updateO(q^3 log n); a fresh O(nq^2) forward pass can be better for few/broad queries. Gaussian fixed-span reuse is ordinary Woodbury; sparse residual sketches require fixed families and known coercivity.
